final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced (on Linux with the open-file limit lowered; the report was on Windows)

**Expected:** `eslint <dir> --fix` writes every fix and exits 0.
**Actual:** the fixes are written all at once, the process runs out of file handles, and ESLint crashes with the same stack as the report. Some files are left unfixed (121 of 1124 in my runs).
```
Error: EMFILE: too many open files, open '.../tmp/emfile-fix-check/file_890.js'
    at async open (node:internal/fs/promises:697:25)
    at async Object.writeFile (node:internal/fs/promises:1317:14)
    at async Promise.all (index 1003)
    at async ESLint.outputFixes (lib/eslint/eslint.js:533:3)
    at async Object.execute (lib/cli.js:637:4)
    at async main (bin/eslint.js:175:19)
```
**Trigger:** more files with fixes than the open-file limit allows. Without `--fix`, linting the same 1101+ files passes with exit 0, because reading files already retries on EMFILE/ENFILE. Writing them doesn't.
**Run:** `node tools/repro-emfile-fix.js` (needs a POSIX shell; it lowers the limit to 1024 only for the ESLint process it starts). It makes 1124 files without a final newline, runs `--fix` with `eol-last`, reports the exit code and how many files were left unfixed, and exits 1 if the bug happens.
**Reliability:** 5 failures in 5 runs on Node 22.11.0 at the given revision (9.30.1).
**Versions:** I checked the published 9.28.0 package and its `outputFixes` writes files the same way, so the reporter's version has the same problem.

**Likely cause:** in lib/eslint/eslint.js (lines 527-547), `outputFixes` starts every `fs.writeFile` at once with no retry. Reading files goes through the `Retrier` from `@humanwhocodes/retry` (around line 742). Fixing it the way the maintainer suggested in the thread — wrapping the write in that same retrier — looks right.

I didn't change any production code. The only new file is tools/repro-emfile-fix.js.
